comparator.name: Human Neuroscience
comparator.academicYear: 2026–2027 adopted OER; prospectus years 2 and 3 expressly provisional
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted OER establishes a 180-EC degree and a complete 60-EC first year, then describes the second year provisionally as five learning lines totalling 60 EC. For the third year it confirms an 18-EC research internship and final project and 26 EC of open elective space; the remaining 16 EC are not assigned a stable formal course/track structure. The provisional public year-three page separately presents 1 EC personal development, 9 EC STEM options and two 6-EC neurocognition/neurotechnology options on top of the 18-EC project and 26-EC free space: 66 rather than its stated 60 EC. These public options cannot all be required as listed while keeping the 26-EC free space. The public year-one page also prints Linear Algebra as 2 EC although the adopted OER assigns 3 EC; the OER figure is used here. Only formally or clearly supported components are retained. No unidentified credits have been invented to force 180 EC.

exception.reason: A coherent year-three 60-EC route cannot be reconstructed from the current official evidence. The adopted 2026–27 OER says the third year is still in development and identifies only the required 18-EC research project and 26 EC of free space. The public prospectus labels the year 60 EC but lists an additional 1 + 9 + 12 EC of personal development, STEM and track choices, which yields 66 EC. Removing a 6-EC choice or reducing free space would be an unsupported curricular decision; a full 180-EC comparator and fair comparison must wait for Radboud to clarify the structure.
exception.curriculumContext: The published 2026–27 OER is controlling for formal requirements. It establishes 60 + 60 EC for years 1 and 2 and confirms 44 EC in year 3, leaving 16 EC whose required/choice status is not determined. The year-three prospectus instead enumerates 66 EC despite its 60-EC heading; its named NeuroCognition and NeuroTechnology choices cannot yet be treated as a verified formal route. The separate year-one Linear Algebra discrepancy is resolved in favour of the OER's 3 EC.
